title: Solve 2 of 10 sealed ARC-AGI-2 training tasks
goal: Treat the ten sealed ARC-AGI-2 training tasks in assets/gc-442/task_ids.txt as a planned batch and get at least two fully solved under cell-exact grading. Triage all ten first: classify each task's apparent transformation family, rank by tractability, and commit an attempt budget before solving anything. Work down the ranking with the hypothesize-verify-predict loop, run the grader at least once mid-batch to confirm the prediction format and the solved count so far, and re-plan after every grader verdict. Tasks left unsolved must be documented by id with the specific rule family that was tried and where it broke, so the failure set is auditable rather than a bare count.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-442/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 10 task ids, one per line; all from the public training split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-442/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-442/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-442/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-442/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-442/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
